newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa introduces money market funds bill.
newsitem.headline: South Africa introduces money market funds bill.

text.p: Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus on Thursday introduced a bill to permit money market funds in South Africa for the first time, saying they would help to counter fraudulent savings schemes.
The Unit Trusts Control Amendment Bill would allow unit trusts to invest solely or partly in money market instruments with a maximum maturity of 12 months.
Money market instruments are short-term securities issued by the central Reserve Bank, commercial banks and other financial institutions.
"An important consideration ... is that... this kind of financial institution will provide the public with an alternative savings mechanism in the short-term money market," Marcus told parliament.
"It will make it more difficult for grey-market operators -- money brokers, bucket shops, pyramid schemes -- to take savings from unknowing small investors," Marcus said.
The bill has still to be discussed by parliament's influential finance committee.

The bill proposes to allow the inclusion of money market instruments in unit trust portfolios, but requires the Registrar of Unit Trust Companies to publish a list of approved instruments after consulting the Unit Trusts Advisory Committee.
The Finance Ministry will draw up rules for the new investment instruments.
Market analysts said they expected parliament to approve the bill soon, but they did not expect the way to be opened for money market funds until the first quarter of next year.
